blocks.x: Lakehouse Architecture & Migration as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

The lakehouse is the convergence point of analytics and AI: one governed copy of data serving BI, feature engineering and GenAI retrieval. We design and migrate estates onto Databricks (Unity Catalog, Delta, MLflow) or Snowflake with the discipline vendors skip: workspace and entitlement design mapped to your org, tag-based access control for sensitive domains, cost governance from day one, and a migration factory that moves pipelines in bounded waves with consumer cutover plans.

Where platforms differ, we say so: we hold implementation partnerships across the major stacks and recommend based on workload profile, existing licenses and team skills — not on resale margin. Every migration ends with an operating handbook: release trains, environment strategy, cost showback and a capability path toward self-service under governance.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
